title: routing-auth-snaglist-and-synth
content:
Meeting: Routing/Auth quick triage + weekly synthesis (informal)
Date: 2027-07-28
Facilitator: Samir Patel
Attendees: Samir, Mei, Jordan, Elena, Devon (+ async notes from Priya)
Duration: 35m (quick sync)

Purpose / Context
- Follow up on 2027-07-27 late-night quota/auth anomalies that surfaced in hosted API (spikes in 429s tied to token refresh path). Short-term mitigation was applied; this doc captures the triage, root cause hypotheses, immediate cleanups, and the next-phase engineering work.
- Also use the moment to synthesize routing+auth small backlog items we want to prioritize next sprint (routing fallthroughs, auth token caching bug, quota accounting drift for dedicated customers).

Quick summary / tl;dr
- Incident: sharp increase in auth-related 429s between ~02:12–03:03 UTC, primarily affecting CSAT tier 3 customers and a few dedicated pools. Root cause: token-refresh path was not respecting a per-customer in-flight limit; a change in allocator routing combined with retry storm produced a hot-key on our KMS proxy and quota metering.
- Mitigation: turned on conservative per-customer in-flight cap in routing for 2h (quick config flip), deployed temporary rate-limit backpressure in front of token-refresh service. 429 spike resolved. Customers notified via status page.
- Next: patch in controlplane to gate token-refresh using a leaky-bucket per-customer (PLTFM-3421), add metrics and tracing for refresh latency + queue length, and evaluate longer term: move token refresh to a sidecar cache per pod for dedicated pools.

Notes / timeline (raw)
- 02:05 UTC: SRE alert - increase in 429s from /v1/token/refresh. Error samples show 'quota_exceeded' from our internal KMS proxy.
- 02:12 UTC: routing team noticed sudden bump in single-customer traffic to refresh endpoint (customer A). The allocator change earlier in the week (reducing route fanout for GPU pools) increased the per-VM request concentration for that customer on a handful of pods.
- 02:18 UTC: retries from clients (exponential backoff misconfigured earlier) amplified load; refresh backend queued many requests; KMS proxy started returning 429 to protect downstream; internal quota accounting reported unexpected negative drift.
- 02:30 UTC: mitigations applied — set route-level in-flight cap = 10 for token-refresh route; enabled short-circuit 503 backoff for retried clients. 429s drop immediately.
- 02:45 UTC: paging/larger team notified. Observed tail latency on refresh path increase even for unaffected customers due to shared KMS proxy resource.
- 03:03 UTC: incident quieted; continued monitoring; flagged for post-incident follow-up.

Root cause hypotheses (from triage)
- Primary: Missing per-customer in-flight limit on the token-refresh endpoint combined with allocator routing that concentrated traffic. This created a hot-spot: many concurrent refresh requests from one customer hit same KMS proxy instance -> proxy applied protective rate-limiting -> upstream 429s.
- Secondary: retry/backoff behavior in some SDK clients was too aggressive (we had a partial roll of new retry policy in client library); combined with short TTLs for refresh tokens, this increased request rate.
- Tertiary/observability gap: we lacked granular metrics for 'refresh queue length' and per-pod KMS-proxy saturation, making the problem appear as a quota drift instead of a concentrated hotkey.

Decisions made in sync
- Short-term config: keep the conservative per-customer in-flight cap on routing.token-refresh for 48h while we validate traffic patterns (Samir applied already).
- Medium-term fix: implement per-customer leaky-bucket in controlplane and gate token-refresh calls (ticket PLTFM-3421). This will prevent single-customer storms from affecting shared KMS proxies.
- Observability: add refresh_queue_length, refresh_backpressure_events, and per-kms-proxy saturation gauge in the next metrics sprint (owner: Mei).
- Client-side: revert the partially rolled retry aggressiveness change and coordinate with DX to publish guidance/patch for SDKs (owner: Jordan).
- Dedicated pools: design and prototype per-pod sidecar cache for refresh tokens for Dedicated customers to reduce cross-customer coupling (owner: Elena + Solutions eng).

Action items (with owners & rough ETA)
- PLTFM-3421: Controlplane leaky-bucket for token-refresh per-customer — owner: Devon — due: 2027-08-11
- Add refresh queue metrics and Grafana panels (dashboard PR) — owner: Mei — due: 2027-08-04
- Revert client retry policy and prepare SDK patch + changelog — owner: Jordan — due: 2027-08-02
- Design doc: sidecar-token-cache for Dedicated pools (10% latency improvement target, reduces KMS calls) — owner: Elena — draft due: 2027-08-09
- Run dedicated-customer smoke test with artificial high-refresh load in staging to validate caps — owner: Samir — due: 2027-08-06
- Post-incident writeup for status page + internal blameless summary — owner: Samir — due: 2027-07-30

Related small backlog items (sprint grooming candidates)
- routing: fallthrough routing rule test coverage gap (flaky in CI) — add 2 tests — est: 1d
- auth: quota accounting negative drift edge-case when KMS returns partial errors — root-cause deeper inspect — est: 2d
- infra: KMS proxy autoscaling threshold is too coarse — make it look at p95 CPU and request queue length — est: 2d

Diagnostics/observability snippets (raw findings)
- Sample trace: trace-id=trf-7a5c refreshed 480 requests in 3m, peak concurrency ~120 on two pods, p99 latency 1.2s -> KMS proxy errors started when concurrency > 60.
- Logs: KMS proxy emitted logs showing quota window: "quota window exceeded for client-key 0xA3 at 2027-07-28T02:14:12Z" — matched client A refresh spikes.
- Dashboard: saw correlation between allocator fanout change on 2027-07-22 and initial higher variance in per-pod traffic distribution for certain customers.

Risk notes
- If we over-aggressively cap in-flight refresh requests, customers with legitimate burst patterns (e.g., background syncs) will see higher latency/refresh failures. Need to expose cap per-customer profile and allow overrides for Dedicated with SLA.
- Sidecar cache approach adds complexity (deployment surface and key rotation semantics). Evaluate KMS key caching TTL semantics with security/compliance team before wide rollout.

Customer communications
- Status page update posted at 03:20 UTC summarizing impact and mitigation. Template sent to CS for follow-up with affected accounts. (Samir to craft one-paragraph summary for CS)

Open questions
- Should we make token-refresh idempotent and collapse duplicate refreshes for the same session (i.e., only one inflight refresh per session key)? Pros: reduces load. Cons: complexity for SDKs and session semantics.
- For Dedicated customers, is sidecar cache acceptable from security posture? (bring in security/compliance to evaluate).

Notes to self / ephemeral thoughts (shorthand)
- Need to check if older allocator change that reduced cross-pool fanout is still net-positive for latency/cost; maybe it increased fragility for hot customers. Flag for allocator retro.
- We should have a small runbook entry for token-refresh storms (playbook: cap -> backpressure -> sidecar deploy flow).

Next steps / follow-up meeting
- Quick check-in 2027-08-02 to validate progress on metrics + SDK revert.
- Full incident RCA scheduled 2027-08-06 with SRE/observability to finalize root cause and permanent mitigations.

Raw references (tickets/PRs/dashboards)
- PLTFM-3421 (controlplane token-refresh gate)
- PR: controlplane/pull/6142 (initial leaky-bucket prototype - WIP)
- Grafana panel: Routing -> token-refresh heatmap

End of notes.
